families.constitution: intent != plan != requirement != acceptance != observed outcome
families.title: Enterprise intent, outcome, constraint and acceptance
families.vision: Translate an authorized desired change into falsifiable outcomes, bounded constraints and acceptance evidence without confusing goals, measures or plans.

families.constitution: identifier != identity; proof of control != subject identity; same spelling != same referent
families.title: Identifier, identity, namespace, version and resolution
families.vision: Name, resolve and track subjects across scopes and time while preserving ambiguity, authority and lifecycle rather than pretending identifier equality proves identity.

families.constitution: instant != local date-time; duration != calendar period; valid time != recording or transaction time
families.title: Temporal position, interval, calendar, clock and database time
families.vision: Represent when things occur, apply, are observed and are recorded using explicit temporal reference systems, uncertainty and ordering guarantees.

families.constitution: number != quantity; probability != confidence or score; missing != zero; censored != missing
families.title: Quantity, unit, scale, money, ratio, probability and partial information
families.vision: Carry magnitudes with dimensions, units, scales, uncertainty and information-state semantics so arithmetic cannot silently erase meaning.

families.constitution: authority != responsibility; approval != issuance; policy decision != enforcement; authentication != authorization
families.title: Authority, ownership, delegation, entitlement and policy precedence
families.vision: Determine who may decide, issue, delegate, enforce or revoke a capability for a scoped purpose and time without collapsing responsibility or evidence into authority.

families.constitution: recommendation != decision; decision != action; action != effect; observation != causal effect
families.title: Governed decision, action, feedback and effect authority
families.vision: Turn qualified evidence and policy into governed decisions, separately authorized actions, observed effects and learning feedback with explicit refusal and compensation.

non_collapsible_distinctions.law: An identifier is a scoped symbol; identity is the set of attributes and relations by which a subject is recognized in a domain.
Control of a credential or key proves control under a method, not who or what the subject is.
Lexical equality without scheme, namespace, version and time cannot establish co-reference.
Equal digests under one canonical representation do not establish semantic equality under another model.
A merge is an authorized lifecycle action; it does not prove all historical assertions were equivalent.
An alias preserves a mapping claim and its authority; it is not silently rewritten into canonical identity.
A local date-time needs a calendar, zone rule or offset and disambiguation before it can denote an instant.
Elapsed seconds and calendar months have different arithmetic and cannot be freely substituted.
When a claim applies differs from when a system learned or stored it.
Occurrence time and processing time support different window, lateness and correction laws.
A wall-clock reading cannot by itself prove happens-before in a distributed system.
An offset is one result of versioned zone rules at an instant; it is not the zone.
A scalar without quantity kind, unit and scale cannot participate safely in domain arithmetic.
Quantities with unit one can still have distinct quantity kinds and interpretation.
Probability requires a sample space and semantics; confidence may denote procedure coverage or informal belief.
A score need not be calibrated, additive or probabilistic.
Absence of a value is not the additive identity.
Censoring carries a known bound or observation mechanism; generic missingness does not.
Closeness to a reference and repeatability are different properties.
Money additionally requires currency, minor-unit, valuation-time and rounding policy.
The desired change does not prescribe a single realization unless explicitly constrained.
A measure supplies evidence about a goal; it is not the desired state itself.
A normative statement and evidence that it was satisfied remain separately identifiable.
An assumption is challengeable and must carry a falsifier or review trigger.
Conformance to specification differs from fitness for the intended use.
Being accountable for work does not necessarily grant power to authorize it.
Approval is a decision; issuance creates a grant or artifact and requires separate effect authority.
A permit result has no effect until an authorized enforcement point applies it.
Evidence about a principal does not establish permission for an action.
Title or control and delegated care obligations have different lifecycles and powers.
Removing authority or status is not erasing the historical record.
A recommendation proposes; a decision commits an authorized decision-maker under policy.
A decision is a governed conclusion; an action changes or attempts to change the world.
Command success or action completion does not prove the intended effect occurred.
An observation is a method- and time-qualified assertion, not reality itself.
Observed association does not identify the counterfactual effect of intervention.
Rollback restores prior technical state where possible; compensation is a domain action for irreversible work.
